summary: `loom factory close <order> --shipped-by <url>` currently refuses any order outside PhaseParked or PhaseStopped. The saturday-monorepo pilot hit this when order `reagent-map-save` was finished by hand while the factory's own run was still waiting at a confirm-ship gate: the only way out was to approve the commit and PR anyway, then close the duplicate PR unmerged. This feature widens closeable()'s allow-list in internal/factory/control.go to also accept PhaseWaiting (waiting at a run gate), PhaseCompleted (waiting for its commit to be approved), and PhaseProposed (waiting for its pull request to be approved) — the three phases where an order is waiting on a human with no process of its own running. Every other phase (claimed, running, retrying, committed, pushed, shipped) stays refused exactly as today. Because inbox.go's itemsFor, finish.go's finishStep, and start.go's continuationKind all switch on Phase with no PhaseShipped case, closing one of these orders automatically drops it from the inbox and stops the supervisor from ever committing, pushing, proposing, or relaunching it again — no code change is needed in those three files, only tests proving it. The only other changes are documentation: the close command's help text and the intake README's 'order finished by hand' section must name the phases close now accepts.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Given an order waiting at a run gate (waiting), waiting for its commit to be approved (completed), or waiting for its pull request to be approved (proposed), closing it with `loom factory close <order> --shipped-by <url>` records it shipped exactly as a parked order today: one shipped ledger entry with the URL and approvedBy, then the run archived and the worktree removed.

After closing a waiting, completed, or proposed order, `loom factory inbox` no longer lists it, nothing is committed or pushed for it, and no pull request is opened for it — even if an approval for it was already in the ledger and not yet acted on.

An order whose run process is alive (running), one between a commit and its pull request (committed, pushed), or one scheduled to retry (retrying) still refuses close with exit code 1 and the phase named; the ledger does not change. An already-shipped order is refused as today.
With the supervisor ticking, closing a waiting order and then running one more supervisor tick never relaunches, commits, or proposes that order again.
examples: A unit test closes a waiting order, calls the test harness's tick() once more, and asserts the ledger gains no launch/commit/push/propose entry.

edgeCases.case: An order is waiting at a run gate (PhaseWaiting) when close runs.
edgeCases.handling: closeable accepts it; Close appends one shipped entry with the URL/approver, archives the run state, and removes the worktree, identically to today's parked/stopped path.

edgeCases.case: An order is completed and awaiting a commit approval (PhaseCompleted), with an unacted-on commit-gate Approval already in the ledger.
edgeCases.handling: closeable accepts it regardless of the pending Approval; after the shipped entry is recorded, finishStep's switch has no PhaseShipped case, so the supervisor never commits the tree on a later tick, even though applyShipped never explicitly clears OrderState.Approval.

edgeCases.case: An order is a proposed pull request awaiting the open-pr approval (PhaseProposed), with that approval already given.
edgeCases.handling: closeable accepts it; openApprovedPR's switch excludes PhaseShipped, so the supervisor never opens the pull request on a later tick — the stale approval is simply never acted on again.

edgeCases.case: The order's run process is still alive (PhaseRunning), it is between a commit and its pull request (PhaseCommitted, PhasePushed), or it is scheduled to retry (PhaseRetrying).
edgeCases.handling: closeable still refuses with ErrNotApplicable, naming the phase and instructing the operator to stop it first; the ledger is unchanged, matching today's behavior for every phase outside the allow-list.
closeable still refuses, naming the phase and noting it has already shipped, exactly as today — PhaseShipped is never added to the allow-list.

edgeCases.case: The supervisor ticks once right after close runs on a waiting/completed/proposed order.
edgeCases.handling: continuationKind and finishStep both switch on Phase with no PhaseShipped case, so pendingWork finds no continuation and finishPass finds no step; the order is not relaunched, committed, pushed, or proposed again.

edgeCases.case: Whether PhaseRetrying should be closeable, raised as an open question in the spec.
edgeCases.handling: Resolved by the spec's own stated assumption: no — a retry can relaunch at any tick, so a person stops it first, the same as a running order.
